newsitem.title: NORWAY: Record nominations for 1997 Nobel Peace Prize.
newsitem.headline: Record nominations for 1997 Nobel Peace Prize.

text.p: Norway's Nobel Committee said on Tuesday it expected to have a record number of nominations to consider when it sits for its first meeting to shortlist candidates for this year's Nobel Peace Prize.
Geir Lundestad, director of the committee, said so far the institute had received 125 different nominations -- valid if postmarked before February 1 -- including 25 for organisations.

"We are still receiving nominations and the committee members can also nominate a candidate at the first meeting, so we expect the number to exceed 130, which will be a new record," Lundestad told Reuters.
The committee will gather for a preliminary session on February 25. It will meet five to six times in all before it announces a decision in mid-October.
The 1996 Nobel Peace Prize was awarded to two East Timor human rights campaigners, Roman Catholic Bishop Carlos Belo and self-exiled activist Jose Ramos Horta.
Lundestad said around three-quarters of nominations had been proposed before.
"There is undoubtedly growing interest in the Peace Prize and we see a continued global focus. We have worked hard to make this a truly global prize," Lundestad said.
True to its commitment not to reveal the names of Nobel candidates, the committee refuses to confirm any nomination.
However, this year's list is known to include jailed Chinese dissident Wei Jingsheng, who was put forward by a little-known Brussels-based Transnational Radical Party.

Earlier this month the the International PEACE Bureau (IPB) said it had nominated Vesna Pesic, a leader of Serbia's opposition coalition, Selim Beslagic, the mayor of the Bosnian city of Tuzla and Vesna Terselic, a peace activist from Croatia.
Other likely candidates are believed to be former U.S. President Jimmy Carter and the Salvation Army.
